subject: Veterans Day
hook: VETERANS DAY IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Veterans Day is officially spelled without an apostrophe because the holiday is meant to honor all veterans rather than belonging to them.
angle_support: the United States Department of Veterans Affairs website states that the attributive (no apostrophe) rather than the possessive case is the official spelling
because it is not a day that 'belongs' to veterans, it is a day for honoring all veterans.
title: Why Veterans Day Has No Apostrophe
description: The holiday’s name isn’t possessive. Official guidance explains the spelling skips the apostrophe to stress that the day honors, not belongs to, veterans. Learn the exact reason behind the punctuation choice.
narration: VETERANS DAY IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You assume the holiday belongs to veterans, like a possessive celebration. In fact, the name uses an attributive form, meaning it honors them, not owned by them in everyday language today. The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs states the official spelling omits the apostrophe because the day does not belong to veterans; it is a day for honoring all veterans, as confirmed in the agency’s style guide in its official communications. So the spelling stays plain—no apostrophe, just respect for the nation today.
